recent_posts.title:
Anthropic claims to be a “safety and research” company building “reliable, interpretable, steerable” AI systems. 

but Dario’s branding around AI safety is not convincing anymore. it has caused so much doomerism which btw, has yielded massive profit for them.

Claude has its fair share of nuking databases and leakages, nothing uniquely “safe” about it than any other model out there. nothing publicly uniquely different about how they’re training their models either.

the safety and interpretability papers are nice, but they don’t compensate for the daily dose of scare tactics. 

Dario claimed that AI safety was one of the major reasons he left OpenAI. fine. 

what has he done differently?
what’s so specially safe about Claude?
most importantly, what does he expect the public, the general white collar dude to do when he keeps repeating AI will replace you in X months? 

I used to believe Anthropic is the sensible player and OpenAI thrives on drama and fear, but it seems like the tables have turned massively.
recent_posts.summary: A critical take on Anthropic and its CEO Dario Amodei's AI safety branding. The author argues that Anthropic's 'safety-first' positioning is increasingly unconvincing, functioning more as a marketing strategy and fear-mongering tactic than a genuine differentiator. Claude is noted to have the same failure modes as other models, and the safety/interpretability research doesn't offset the doomerism rhetoric that has proven commercially profitable for the company.
